policy_title: Review the Online Safety Bill regarding free speech
stated: Reform UK will review the Online Safety Bill, asserting that social media giants pushing 'baseless transgender ideology and divisive Critical Race theory' should have no role in regulating free speech.

source.quote: Review the Online Safety Bill Social media giants that push baseless transgender ideology and divisive Critical Race theory should have no role in regulating free speech.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly concerns the free expression framework — reviewing legislation that governs online speech regulation — which is squarely within O9's civil-liberties (speech) scope and would earn a real verdict on whether the legal/regulatory framework protecting or restricting free expression is strengthened or weakened.

Reviewing the Online Safety Bill with the stated aim of reducing platforms' role in speech regulation directly bears on freedom of expression and freedom from state/platform coercion online — a core O10 indicator.

membership_note: Two genuine bearings: O10 (liberty/speech gain if regulation is rolled back) and O9 (equal-treatment harm if protections for minority groups are weakened) — these are rival goods, which is the normal tension between O10 and O9 and justifies both being in the bearing-set.
